newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on wheat gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on wheat gains.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed on Friday with nearbys up on strong gains in wheat and on rumors of a drop in deliverable soy stocks, traders said.

Floor sources cited rumors two commercial grain firms planned to move roughly 600,000 bushels of soybeans out of Toledo deliverable points. The rumor sparked gains in the May contract ahead of first notice day on April 30.

Support also came from the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush figure. NOPA on Thursday said the weekly U.S. soybean crush was at 26.2 million bushels, near the high end of expectations for 25.5 million to 26.5 million.
Some floor sources perceived last week's sharp drop in crushing levels as an indication demand was tapering off. A slight increase this week put those ideas on hold.
"The crush was good. Some people said it was going down and it was at the high end of expectations plus yesterday's export number was good," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soybean futures closed 5-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 4-1/2 cents lower with May up 5-1/2 at $8.44 a bushel.
New crop months were hit by forecasts for cool weather. The slow spring warm-up led to ideas spring corn plantings will be delayed.
Trade sources cited speculation farmers would be forced to switch intended corn acreage to soybeans if the cold spring prevented on-time plantings, traders said.
Soybeans can be planted later in the year than corn without signficant yield losses, agronomists say.

A port strike in Brazil drew mixed reaction with most trade sources focusing on news Paranagua's stevedores did not participate in the national stoppage. Paranagua ships more soybeans and soymeal than other Brazilian ports.

On the day, LIT America bought four million bushels July and 1.5 million May while Refco Inc bought 2.5 million July, pit sources said. Lee B. Stern sold two million bushels November and Smith Barney sold at least two million July.
Goldenberg-Hehmeyer spread 1.5 million bushels July/November at $1.54 to $1.55, premium July. The July/November spread closed at $1.59-1/2, premium July, up 5-1/2 cents from Thursday.
In options, Merrill Lynch sold 500 November $6.50 puts at 23 cents while Louis Dreyfus bought 250 Nov $8.00 calls at 16 cents and sold 250 Nov $6.75 puts at 36 cents, traders said.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 70,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 64,721.
